title: field-eng customer blocker deep dive - 2026-09-06
content:
Meeting: SolutionsEng + ProServices weekly sync (deep-dive variant)
Date: 2026-09-06 09:00 PT
Facilitator: Priya Nair
Note-taker: Marco Alvarez
Attendees: Priya Nair, Marco Alvarez, Arielle Chen, Ethan Marsh, Samira Patel, Jonah Liu (SRE), Clara Gomez (Customer Success)
Duration: 45m

Purpose: Focused triage of active customer blockers that threaten go-live windows this quarter. This doc captures raw standup-style updates, technical notes from the triage, decisions, and concrete action items with owners and deadlines.

Agenda:
- Quick status (per-customer) 5m
- Blocker deep dives (KV cache, VPC peering, model mismatch, OSS dependency) 30m
- Decisions & mitigations 5m
- Action items & next checks 5m

High-level status (one-line):
- Lighthouse Health: At-risk (network + cert pinning)
- NovaRetail: On-track but performance regressions on long-tail prompts
- CatalystPay: Blocked by DAG conversion and inference pipeline alignment
- AtlasLegal: Rollout paused pending HSM access and audit

Detailed standup notes (raw):
1) Lighthouse Health (Go-live target: 2026-09-20)
- Owner: Clara Gomez (CS) / Jonah Liu (SRE)
- Update: Customer reports intermittent TLS handshake failures when connecting from their VPC to our private endpoint. Failures spike during rolling deploys.
- Triage notes: Jonah reproduced the handshake flakiness in staging using their network snapshot. Observed MTU/path-MTU mismatches and a TLS renegotiation triggered by our healthcheck probe (older OpenSSL behavior) causing connection resets.
- Temporary mitigation: Disable aggressive healthcheck renegotiate and instruct deployment team to use single-connection health probes. Applied to staging only.
- Long-term fix: Coordinate with infra to force TLS 1.3 only and update load balancer config to respect client TTL. Need infra PR and a canary deploy window.
- Risk: If not fixed before go-live, periodic 2–3% error-rate spikes expected, possible customer SLA breach.
- Blocker severity: P1 (high)

2) NovaRetail (Go-live target: 2026-10-01)
- Owner: Arielle Chen (Solutions)
- Update: Early performance testing shows 12% higher p95 latency for long-form product-description prompts when using the quantized variant (4-bit) vs fp16 baseline.
- Investigation: Likely due to attention kernel fallback for sequences > 1024 and suboptimal pad handling causing cache reloads. Reproduced on both A100 and T4 fleet.
- Notes: Experimented with a short-term model config: force sequence chunking and increase KV cache warmup to pre-allocate. That reduced p95 by ~6% but added 3% cost.
- Decision: For initial rollout, use fp16-compatible variant for the first 2 weeks while infra implements a kernel path optimization and batch shape normalization.
- Action: Ethan to open infra ticket for kernel fallback profiling (INFRA-904). Arielle to update rollout plan and CSP.
- Blocker severity: P2 (medium)

3) CatalystPay (Go-live target: 2026-09-30)
- Owner: Samira Patel (ProServices)
- Update: Customer uses a DAG-based preprocessor that emits tensors in a format our runtime doesn't accept (endianness + padding differences). Their CI fails at model load step.
- Triage: Short-term conversion script authored (python) to translate tensors; works but not performant. Root cause is mismatch in serialization stemming from a custom upstream numpy build.
- Mitigation plan: Ship conversion script in customer adapter container as a stopgap. Parallel work: add a native conversion path in runtime that handles both endian and padding at load time (requires runtime change + regression tests).
- Action: Samira to deliver adapter container by 2026-09-10; Runtime team to estimate PR size (expected ~3 sprints).
- Blocker severity: P1 -> schedule-sensitive

4) AtlasLegal (Go-live target: TBD)
- Owner: Priya Nair
- Update: Enterprise compliance requires HSM-backed key wrapping. Customer audit schedule moved up; our Private deployment package currently supports AWS KMS but not the customer's on-prem HSM appliance.
- Notes: Security has flagged additional logging requirements and a signed attestation process.
- Action: Security + Private Deploys to scope HSM connector; legal to draft updated DPA rider.
- Blocker severity: P2 (compliance)

Triage deep-dive highlights (technical):
- KV cache warmup heuristics: Observed that rare prompt prefixes trigger cache thrashing. Proposed new heuristic: maintain probabilistic LRU favoring prefixes above a 0.7 reuse probability threshold. Marco sketching pseudo-code; will spike in staging.
- Network: For TLS issues, recommend rolling back to TLS 1.3-only and pinning cipher suites to avoid renegotiation. Jonah to coordinate LB change and schedule maintenance window (target 2026-09-12).
- Runtime loader: Add permissive tensor loader shim to accept both big/little-endian and a padding flag; compatibility tests will live in runtime/integration/testdata.
- Canary strategy: For Lighthouse and NovaRetail, use a 1% traffic canary with extended telemetry (token-level latency, handshake failures) for 48h before full rollout.

Decisions made:
- NovaRetail will start on fp16 variant for initial 14-day window.
- Lighthouse health TLS change approved; canary window scheduled 2026-09-12 to 2026-09-14.
- CatalystPay: adapter container approach approved as stopgap; runtime change prioritized in next sprint.
- AtlasLegal: Compliance gating will be codified; discovery doc due 2026-09-09.

Action items (owner — due):
- Jonah Liu — submit LB/TLS change PR and schedule canary (due 2026-09-10)
- Ethan Marsh — create INFRA-904 profiling ticket + attach kernel traces (due 2026-09-08)
- Marco Alvarez — prototype KV cache warmup heuristic in staging (due 2026-09-13)
- Samira Patel — publish CatalystPay adapter container and verification steps (due 2026-09-10)
- Priya Nair — draft AtlasLegal discovery & coordinate Legal/Security sync (due 2026-09-09)
- Arielle Chen — update NovaRetail rollout runbook and alerting thresholds (due 2026-09-07)

Follow-ups & checkpoints:
- Quick sync 2026-09-08 (15m) to confirm infra PRs and Catalyst adapter status.
- Full triage review 2026-09-13 to assess canary results and pick next actions.

Notes to self / raw observations:
- Need standardized template for 'adapter container' deliverables (spec, acceptance tests, perf budget).
- Flag: rolling deploys + aggressive health probes = recurring class of TLS/connection issues; add to infra reliability radar.
- Consider adding a 'compatibility checklist' for customer preflight that includes serialization format, expected p95 for 2 sample prompt types, and network MTU checks.

Attachments / linked refs:
- Staging logs archive: s3://redwood-staging/lh-handshake-2026-09-05.tar.gz
- CatalystPay conversion script gist: https://gist.github.com/samira/catalyst-convert

Next meeting: 2026-09-13 09:00 PT — focus: canary results + runtime PR estimation

End of notes. (raw, working doc — will refine for exec summary after canary results)
